title: Provisional cast-on with crochet chain
subtitle: A temporary foundation that leaves live stitches to pick up later.
excerpt: The crochet-chain provisional cast-on anchors stitches in a length of waste yarn that can be unzipped later, releasing live loops for grafting, border pickup, or seamless joins.
sourceNotes: Technique in common use across British and American knitting practice since the mid-twentieth century. Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) covers provisional methods under 'temporary cast-on'. Requires basic crochet chain knowledge.

glossaryTerms.definition: Any cast-on method that anchors stitches temporarily in waste yarn, allowing the waste yarn to be removed later to release live loops.
A length of smooth, slippery yarn in a contrasting colour used as a temporary placeholder. Removed once the live stitches have been picked up on the working needles.
Stitches that are not yet cast off; they can be placed back onto a needle and worked further.

that were sitting in its chain. These can be grafted to another set of live stitches, picked up for a border worked in the opposite direction, or joined in any way the pattern requires. Difficulty: intermediate, because it requires a crochet hook and a little patience unzipping the waste yarn at the end.
Working yarn and 4 mm knitting needles
Smooth waste yarn in a contrasting colour (slippery cotton works well)
Crochet hook approximately the same size as the knitting needles
With the crochet hook and waste yarn, make a slip knot and crochet a chain of several more stitches than you need to cast on. Fasten off loosely.
Turn the chain over so the bumps on the back face upward.

With the knitting needle and your working yarn, pick up one stitch through each bump in the crochet chain until you have the required number of stitches. Pick up from the first full bump, not the slip knot end.
Knit the piece as directed by your pattern.

When you are ready to release the live stitches, find the slip-knot end of the crochet chain and pull it gently. The chain will unzip one loop at a time. Slide each released loop onto a knitting needle as it appears.

Provisional cast-ons appear in seamless construction (a top-down yoke may cast on provisionally at the hem so the front and back hems can be grafted), in shawl patterns that work from the centre outward, and in double-knit projects that begin from a fold. The grafting step uses the Kitchener graft.

items.symptom: Chain unzips but no stitches are released
items.cause: Picking up through the wrong side of the chain or through the V rather than the bump
items.fix: Ensure you picked up through the bumps on the back of the chain. If you went through the V side, the stitches will be locked in.

items.symptom: Stitches released in the wrong direction (sitting on the needle twisted)
items.cause: Picking up in the opposite direction to how they were formed
items.fix: As each stitch is released, check which leg sits on the front of the needle and correct any twisted ones before knitting across.

items.cause: Not making enough extra chain stitches
items.fix: Always chain at least 5-10 stitches more than you need. The excess is cut away; running short forces you to start over.
